{{Otheruses}}
{{Unreferenced|date=August 2014}}
{{nihongo|Natsumatsuri|夏祭り|1=Natsu Matsuri}} refers to the general term for {{ill|Summer Matsuri|ja|夏祭り|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11430090}} held in {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|qid=Q17|lt=Japan}}. These festivals are typically held from early July to late August, although festivals held in September that correspond to the {{ill|Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|ja|旧暦}}'s {{ill|July (Lunisolar)|ja|7月 (旧暦)|lt=seventh month}} are often treated as summer festivals<ref>Examples include Kimata Town Fireworks Festival and Arima Town Bon Dance.</ref>.

== Overview ==
Many of Japan's summer festivals are rooted in events such as {{ill|Ullambana Festival|ja|盂蘭盆会|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q15898039}} (盂蘭盆会), {{ill|Qixi Festival|en|Qixi Festival|qid=Q13423122|lt=Tanabata}}, and {{ill|Gion Matsuri|en|Gion Matsuri|qid=Q979873|lt=Gion Matsuri}}, or related rituals. As such, these festivals align with the sixth and seventh months of the old lunisolar calendar. In rural areas, these events often originated as part of relieving labor fatigue from summer farming activities. In urban areas, they are believed to stem from pre-{{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}} traditions of warding off summer epidemics and honoring the dead.

However, modernization has caused significant transformations in these festivals, and their origins are often not recognized. Summer festivals are now largely regarded as vibrant and festive events rather than solemn ones. Furthermore, many festivals lack origins before the Edo period, having been introduced in the modern era or modeled after traditional festivals from other regions.

Especially around the {{ill|Ullambana Festival|ja|盂蘭盆会|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q15898039}} season in August, summer festivals are often associated with homecoming, creating opportunities for emotional reunions with loved ones{{Citation needed|date=October 2014}}.

In port towns, variations rich in local flavor, such as "Minato Matsuri" (harbor festivals), are common. Many {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} festivals also take place during this period.
